provenance: Senses that differ by region, language or culture. These are the highest-stakes alternate usages in the set, because the same glyph can be neutral in one country and obscene in another. Gesture divergences are documented in cross-cultural communication literature and in Unicode's own guidance on gesture emoji.

👌.gloss: In Brazil, Turkey and parts of the Mediterranean and Middle East the ring gesture is an insult roughly equivalent to a raised middle finger.
Appropriated as a hate signal from around 2017. The Anti-Defamation League lists it, while noting the overwhelming majority of uses remain innocent.

👍.gloss: Read as an obscene insult in parts of the Middle East, West Africa and South America.

🤙.gloss: A Hawaiian greeting of goodwill; elsewhere read as a telephone gesture. Also appropriated by some far-right groups, complicating its use.

🤘.gloss: The 'corna' implies a man's partner is unfaithful in Italy, Spain and parts of Latin America, quite apart from its rock-music sense.

✌️.gloss: In Britain, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand the palm-inward two fingers is an insult; most emoji fonts render the palm outward, which defuses it.
In Japan, Korea and much of East Asia the V-sign is the default gesture for photographs, carrying no peace-movement meaning.

🙏.gloss: Originates as the Japanese prayer and thanks gesture; the emoji came from Japanese carrier sets, not from Christian prayer imagery.

🖕.gloss: Universally rude but calibrated very differently by culture, and filtered outright by some platforms and keyboards.

🤌.gloss: 'Ma che vuoi' expresses exasperated questioning, a real gesture with real grammar rather than only a meme.

👏.gloss: Clap-between-every-word is an emphatic device online; in some Middle Eastern contexts the gesture itself can read as insulting.

😊.gloss: In Japanese usage smiling emoji often soften a message or mask discomfort, closer to politeness than happiness.

😅.gloss: A common politeness marker in Japanese and Chinese messaging.

🙂.gloss: On WeChat the plain smile has its own strong passive-aggressive reading, sometimes described as 'goodbye to our friendship'.

🌸.gloss: Cherry blossom carries the Japanese aesthetic of mono no aware, impermanence, rather than generic prettiness.

🎋.gloss: The tanabata tree is specific to the Japanese July festival; largely opaque outside Japan.

🎍.gloss: Kadomatsu, a New Year decoration, frequently mistaken for generic bamboo.

🎎.gloss: Japanese Doll Festival dolls, not generic figurines.

🈁.gloss: A squared Japanese ideograph; one of a family of glyphs that are pure signage to Japanese readers and decorative noise to everyone else.

🉐.gloss: Japanese retail signage for a good deal.

💮.gloss: The white flower is a Japanese school marking for excellent work, not a botanical illustration.

🍥.gloss: A specific fish-cake garnish; widely misread as a generic swirl or, in anime fandom, as a Naruto reference.

🍡.gloss: Japanese sweet dumplings, often mistaken for kebabs or lollipops.

🎏.gloss: Koinobori carp streamers flown in May in Japan.

🏮.gloss: The red paper lantern signals a Japanese pub, functioning as a wayfinding sign.

🕉️.gloss: A sacred Hindu, Jain and Buddhist symbol; casual decorative use is read by many as appropriative.

☪️.gloss: Used as a religious identity marker, and consequently a target in harassment campaigns.

✡️.gloss: Identity marker, similarly weaponised in antisemitic harassment.

🇹🇷.gloss: National flag emoji broadly function as diaspora identity, sporting allegiance and political signalling far more than geography.

🏳️.gloss: 'I give up' in argument, not literal capitulation.

🍀.gloss: Frequently stands in for Ireland, though the national emblem is properly the shamrock ☘️.

🥀.gloss: Strongly associated with sad-rap and Arabic-language melancholy posting.

🫱🏻‍🫲🏽.gloss: The two-tone handshake, added in Emoji 14.0, is used deliberately to depict interracial cooperation.

🤝🏿.gloss: Skin-tone-specified handshakes carry a deliberate identity claim absent from the neutral form.
